title: Migration shim
blurb: Simulates Chrome 160's createDTMFSender removal in-tab, installs the blink-dev polyfill shim over RTCRtpSender.dtmf, runs unmodified legacy code on a live loopback, and compares 5 error-parity cases against native.
question: Does the blink-dev createDTMFSender shim over RTCRtpSender.dtmf preserve exact exception names and sender identity when legacy code runs after Chrome 160 removes the method?
result: Verified in Chrome 153 headless: unmodified legacy code works natively, throws TypeError ('pc1.createDTMFSender is not a function') under simulated Chrome 160, works again with the shim installed, and matches native on 5/5 parity cases (TypeError, SyntaxError x2, InvalidStateError, and === sender.dtmf).
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (simulated Chrome 160 removal); not verified on native Chrome 160

friction.summary: Chrome 160 removes RTCPeerConnection.prototype.createDTMFSender with no deprecation period, causing unguarded legacy softphones to throw TypeError
friction.repro: Call pc.createDTMFSender(audioTrack) on Chrome 160+ (or with the Simulate Chrome 160 toggle enabled); execution halts with TypeError: pc.createDTMFSender is not a function.
friction.workaround: Migrate directly to pc.getSenders().find((s) => s.track === audioTrack)?.dtmf, or load the blink-dev RTCPeerConnection.prototype.createDTMFSender shim as an interim bridge.
